verdict: Leads are arriving; a gap in intake means too many aren't being worked.
narrative: Over the last 28 days you received 175 leads at an average cost per lead of $12.15, but the most recent 7 days showed a 15.91% drop in leads alongside a 17.98% rise in cost per lead — a trend that needs to be reversed before it settles in. Separately, your CRM recorded only 147 contacts against those 175 leads, meaning roughly 28 leads did not make it into the pipeline at all, and no opportunities have been created in the system this period. The ads themselves are not the root problem; the intake and follow-up infrastructure — SMS automation, call tracking, and CRM auto-logging — has not yet been fully activated, which is where focus is concentrated right now. Getting those systems live is the condition that turns lead volume into case volume, and that work is in motion this week.

highlights.phrase: leads received from paid ads in the last 28 days
average cost per lead this period
leads this period that did not reach your CRM pipeline

watch_item.issue: Roughly 28 leads per 28-day period are falling out before entering the pipeline, and no leads have converted to tracked opportunities — a direct result of SMS automation, call tracking, and CRM auto-logging not yet being live.
watch_item.fix: These intake tools are being activated now; once live, every inbound lead will be logged, routed, and followed up automatically so pipeline visibility catches up to ad volume.
